G3701.def:
ὀπτασία, -ας, ἡ
(ὀπτάζομαι, Nombres 14:14* = ὀπτάνομαι), later form of ὄψις, [in LXX: Malachie 3:2 (רָאָה ni.), Da TH Daniel 9:23 10:1, 7-8 10:16 (מַרְאֶה, מַרְאָה LXX, ὅραμα, -σις), Esther 4:7, Sir.43:2, 16 * ;] 
__1. an appearing, coming into view (Ma, Es, Sir, ll. with). 
__2. a vision: Luc 1:22 24:23, Actes 26:19, 2 Corinthiens 12:1 (Da, ll. with, also in MGr.).†

G3702.def:
ὀπτός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX: Exode 12:8-9 (צָלִי) * ;] 
roasted, boiled Luc 24:42.†

G3703.def:
ὀπώρα, -ας, ἡ 
[in LXX: Jérémie 48:32 40:10, 12 (קַיִץ) * ;] 
__1. late summer, early autumn (the time between the risings of Sirius and Arcturus, i.e. late July, all August and early September). 
__2. By meton. (as being fruit-time), ripe fruits Apocalypse 18:14 (cf. φθινοπωρινά, Ju 12).†

G3704.def:
ὅπως 
__I. Relat. adv. of manner, as, how: with indic., Luc 24:20. 
__II. Conj., with subjc. (in cl. also with opt., indic.: so in Matthieu 26:59, LT, Tr.), in order that, to the end that, that; 
__1. final, denoting purpose or design (in which the original idea of modality has been merged): after pres., Matthieu 6:2, al.; pf., Actes 9:17, al.; impf., Actes 9:24; aor., Actes 9:2, al.; plpf., Jean 11:57; fut., Matthieu 23:35; imperat., Matthieu 2:8, al.; ὅ. μή (M, Pr., 185), Matthieu 6:18, Luc 16:26, Actes 20:16, 1 Corinthiens 1:29; ὅ. πληρωθῇ, Matthieu 2:23 8:17 13:35; ὅ. ἄν (B1., § 65, 2; WM, § 42, 5), Luc 2:35, Actes 3:19 15:17, Romains 3:4 (cf. Genèse 12:13, Psaumes 59:7. 1Mac 1032, al.). 
__2. After verbs of asking, exhorting, etc.: Matthieu 9:38, Luc 7:3, Jacques 5:16, al. (in late writers its place is often taken by the correl. πῶς, which see)

G3706.def:
ὅρασις, -εως, ἡ
(ὁράω) [in LXX chiefly for מַרְאֶה, חָזוֹן and cognate forms ;] 
__1. in Arist. and later writers, the act of seeing, the sense of sight, and by meton., pl., the eyes. 
__2. appearance (Nombres 24:4, Eze.1:5, Sir.41:20, al.): Apocalypse 4:3. 
__3. = ὅραμα, a vision: Actes 2:17 (LXX), Apocalypse 9:17.†

G3710.def:
ὀργίζω
(ὀργή), [in LXX chiefly for חָרָה, also for קָצַף, etc. ;] 
to make angry, provoke to anger; in cl. most frequently in pass., and so always in NT, to be provoked to anger, be angry: absol., Matthieu 18:34 22:7, Luc 14:21 15:28, Éphésiens 4:26" (LXX), Apocalypse 11:18; with dative, Matthieu 5:22; before ἐπί, with dative (3Ki.11:9, al.), Apocalypse 12:17 (cf. παρ-ὀργίζω).†

G3711.def:
ὀργίλος, -η, -ον
(ὀργή), [in LXX: Proverbes 22:24 29:22 (חֵמָה), etc. ;] 
inclined to anger, passionate: Tite 1:7.†

G3712.def:
ὀργυιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(ὀρέγω), 
the length of the outstretched arms, a fathom: Actes 27:28.†

G3713.def:
ὀρέγω 
[in Sm.: Job 8:20, Eze.16:49 * ;] 
to reach, stretch out; pass. and mid., to stretch oneself out, reach forth; metaphorically, to reach after, grasp at, aspire to: with genitive of thing(s), 1 Timothée 3:1, Hébreux 11:16; φιλαργυρίας (see Ellic. and CGT, in l), 1 Timothée 6:10.†
SYN.: ἐπιθυμέω, to desire (which see)

G3714.def:
ὀρεινός (WH, ὀριν-; see MM, xviii,) -ή, -όν 
(ὄρος), 
mountainous, hilly; ἡ ὀ. (sc. χώρα), the hill-country (LXX for הַר): Luc 1:39, 65 †

G3715.def:
ὄρεξις, -εως, ἡ 
(ὀρέγομαι), [in LXX Wis.14:2 15:5 16:2-3, Sir.18:30 23:6, 4Ma.1:33 4Mac 1:35 * ;] 
the most general ward for all kinds of desire, longing, appetite: of lust, Romains 1:27 
SYN.: see: πάθος

G3716.def:
ὀρθοποδέω, -ῶ
(ὀρθό-πους, going straight), 
= cl. εὐθυπορέω, to walk straight: metaphorically, Galates 2:14 (not elsewhere).†

G3718.def:
ὀρθοτομέω, -ῶ
(- ὀρθός, τέμνω), [in LXX: Proverbes 3:6 11:6 (יָשַׁר pi.)* ;] 
to cut straight, as a road (τ. ὁδούς, figuratively, Pr, ll with). Metaphorical, τ. λόγον τ. ἀληθείας, 2 Timothée 2:15 (V. Ellic. and CGT, in l; not found elsewhere).†

G3719.def:
ὀρθρίζω
(ὄρθρος), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַם hi., Genèse 19:2, al.; also for שָׁחַר pi., Psaumes 63:1, al., etc. ;] 
= cl. poët., ὀρθρεύω, to rise early: before πρός, with accusative of person(s) (as Ps, l.with, al.), Luc 21:38 (see Thumb, Hellen., 123).†

G3720.def:
ὀρθρινός, -ή, -όν
(ὄρθρος), [in LXX: Osée 6:4 13:3 (שָׁכַם hi.), Aggée 2:14, Wis.11:22 * ;] 
late form of ὄρθριος (which see), early: Luc 24:22.†

G3722.def:
ὄρθρος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for שַׁחַר, בֹּקֶר, etc. ;] 
daybreak, dawn: ὄρθρου βαθέως (M, Pr., 73), at early dawn, Luc 24:1; ὄρθρου, Jean 8:2; ὑπὸ τὸν ὄ., Actes 5:21 (cf. MM, xviii).†

G3724.def:
ὁρίζω
(ὅρος, a boundary), [in LXX for אָסַר, גְּבוּל, etc. ;] 
__1. to separate, mark off by boundaries (so Nombres 34:6, Jean 13:27). 
__2. to determine, appoint, designate: of time, with accusative, Actes 17:26, Hébreux 4:7; with accusative of person(s), Actes 17:31; with inf., Actes 11:29; pass., Luc 22:22, Actes 2:23 10:42, Romains 1:4 (cf. ὀφ-, ἀπο- δι-, τρο-ορίζω),†

G3725.def:
ὅριον, -ου, τό
(ὅρος, a boundary), [in LXX chiefly for גְּבוּל ;] 
a boundary, bound; chiefly in pl., and so always in NT: Matthieu 2:16 4:13 8:34 15:22, 39 19:1, Marc 5:17 7:24, 31 10:1, Actes 13:50.†

G3726.def:
ὁρκίζω
(ὅρκος), [in LXX: Genèse 24:37, al. (שָׁבַע hi.) ;] 
__1. to make one swear (Xen., Polyb., a1.). 
__2. to adjure: with dupl. accusative, Marc 5:7, Actes 19:13 (cf. ἐν-, ἐξ-ορκίζω).†

G3727.def:
ὅρκος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁוַע, שִׁבְעָה and cogn. forms ;] 
an oath: Matthieu 14:7 26:72, Luc 1:73, Actes 2:30, Hébreux 6:16-17, Jacques 5:12; p1., Matthieu 5:33 (LXX) Matthieu 14:9, Marc 6:26.†

G3728.def:
ὁρκωμοσία, -ας, ἡ
(ὅρκος, ὄμνυμι; by metapl. for τὰ ὁρκωμόσια, asseverations on oath; see MM, xviii), [in LXX: Eze.17:18-19 (עָלָה) 1Es 9:93* ;] 
affirmation on oath, an oath: Hébreux 7:20-21, 28.†

G3729.def:
ὁρμάω, -ῶ
(ὁρμή), [in LXX for שׁוּב, etc. ;] 
__1. causal, to set in motion, urge on. 
__2. Intrans., to hasten on, rush: before εἰς, Matthieu 8:32, Marc 5:13, Luc 8:33, Actes 19:29; ἐπί, with accusative, Actes 7:57.†

G3730.def:
ὁρμή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX: Proverbes 3:25 (שׁוֹא), etc. ;] 
__1. a violent movement, impulse: Jacques 3:4; 
__2. a hostile movement, onset, assault. Actes 14:5.†

G3731.def:
ὅρμημα, -τος, τό
(ὁρμάω) [in LXX: Osée 5:10, Amos 1:11 (עֶבְרָה), etc. ;] 
a rush: Apocalypse 18:21.†

G3732.def:
ὄρνεον, -ου, τό = ὄρνις, 
[in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר ;] 
a bird: Apocalypse 18:2 19:17, 21 (Hom., al.).†

G3733.def:
ὄρνις, -ιθος, ὁ, ἡ 
[in LXX: ὄ. ἐκλεκταί, I2Ki.3:1 4:23 (3Ki.5:3) (בַּרְבֻּר)* ;] 
a bird; specif., a cock, a hen: Matthieu 23:3, Luc 13:34 (WH).†

G3734.def:
ὁροθεσία, -ας, ἡ
(ὅρος, a boundary, + τίθημι) 
a setting of boundaries; in pl., bounds; Actes 17:26.†

G3735.def:
ὄρος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX chiefly, and very freq., for הַר ;] 
a mountain: Matthieu 4:8 17:1, Marc 9:2, Jean 4:20, 2 Pierre 1:18, al.; opposite to βουνός, Luc 3:5 (LXX); ὄ. τ. ἐλαιῶν, Matthieu 21:1 24:3, al. (see: ἐ.); ὄ. Σιών (Σ., prob. in gem appos.), Hébreux 12:22, Apocalypse 14:1; ὄ. Σινά, Actes 7:30, 38 Galates 4:24-25; τὸ ὄ., of the hill district as distinct from the lowlands, esp. the hills above the Sea of Galilee, Matthieu 5:1 8:1, Marc 3:13 6:46, al.; τὰ ὄ., Matthieu 18:12, Marc 5:5, Hébreux 11:38, Apocalypse 6:14, al.; proverbially (cf. Rabbinic, הדים עקר), of overcoming difficulties, accomplishing marvels, ὄρη μεθιστάνειν, 1 Corinthiens 13:2, cf. Matthieu 17:20 21:21, Marc 11:23

G3736.def:
ὀρύσσω 
[in LXX chiefly for חָפַר also for כָּרָה, etc. ;] 
to dig: with accusative, ληνόν, Matthieu 21:33; ὁπολήνιον, Marc 12:1; γῆν, Matthieu 25:18 (cf. δι-, ἐξ-ορύσσω).†

G3737.def:
ὀρφανός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX for יָתוֹם ;] 
__1. prop., orphan, fatherless: Marc 12:40, WH, mg, Jacques 1:27. 
__2. In a general sense (as also in cl.; see LS, see word; and cf. MM, xviii), bereft, friendless, desolate: Jean 14:18.†

G3738.def:
ὀρχέομαι, -οῦμαι 
[in LXX for רָקַד, etc. ;] 
to dance; Matthieu 11:17 14:6, Marc 6:22, Luc 7:32.†

G3739.def:
ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, 
the postpositive article (ἄρθρον ὑποτακτικόν). 
__I. As demonstr. pron. = οὗτος, ὅδε, this, that, also for αὐτός, chiefly in nom.: ὅς δέ, but he (cf. ἦ δὲ ὅς, frequently in Plat.), Marc 15:23, Jean 5:11; ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, the one . . . the other, Matthieu 21:35, 22:5, 25:15, Luc 23:33, Actes 27:14, Romains 14:5, 1 Corinthiens 11:21, 2 Corinthiens 2:18, Ju 22; neut., ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δέ, the one . . . the other, some . . . some, Matthieu 13:8, 23, Romains 9:21; ὃς (ὃ) μὲν . . . (ἄλλος (ἄλλο)) . . . ἕτερος, Marc 4:4, Luc 8:5, 1 Corinthiens 12:8-10; οὓς μέν, absol., 1 Corinthiens 12:28; ὃς μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, Romains 14:2.
__II. As relat. pron., who, which, what, that; 
__1. agreeing in gender with its antecedent, but differently governed as to case: Matthieu 2:9, Luc 9:9, Actes 20:18, Romains 2:29, al. mult.
__2. In variation from the common construction; 
__(a) in gender, agreeing with a noun in apposition to the antecedent: Marc 15:16, Galates 3:16, Éphésiens 6:17, al.; constr. ad sensum: Jean 6:9, Colossiens 2:19, 1 Timothée 3:16, Apocalypse 13:14, al.; 
__(b) in number, constr. ad sensum: Actes 15:36, 2 Pierre 3:1; 
__(with) in case, by attraction to the case of the antecedent (Bl., §50, 2): Jean 4:18, Actes 3:21, Romains 15:18, 1 Corinthiens 6:19, Éphésiens 1:8, al. 
__3. The neut. ὅ with nouns of other gender and with phrases, which thing, which term: Marc 3:17 12:42, Jean 1:39, Colossiens 3:14, al.; with a sentence, Actes 2:32, Galates 2:10, 1 Jean 2:8, al. 
__4. With ellipse of a demonstrative (οὗτος or ἐκεῖνος), before or after: before, Matthieu 20:23, Luc 7:43, Romains 10:14, al.; after, Matthieu 10:38, Marc 9:40, Jean 19:22, Romains 2:1 al. 
__5. Expressing purpose, end or cause: Matthieu 11:10 (who = that he may), Marc 1:2, Hébreux 12:6 al. 
__6. C. prep, as periphrasis for conjc.: ἀνθ᾽ ὧν ( = ἀντὶ τούτων ὧν), because, Luc 1:20, al.; wherefore, Luc 12:3; ἐξ οὗ, since, for that, Romains 5:12; ἀφ᾽ οὗ, since (temporal), Luc 13:25; ἐξ οὗ, whence, Philippiens 3:20; etc. 
__7. With particles: ὃς ἄν (ἐάν), see: ἄν, ἐάν; ὃς καί, Marc 3:19, Jean 21:20, Romains 5:2, al.; ὃς καὶ αὐτός, Matthieu 27:57. 
__8. Gen., οὗ, absol., as adv. (see: οὗ).

G3740.def:
ὁσάκις
(ὅσος), 
relat. adv., 
as often as: before ἐάν (which see), 1 Corinthiens 11:25-26, Apocalypse 11:6,†

G3741.def:
ὅσιος, -ον
(so sometimes in cl., but most frequently -α, -ον), [in LXX chiefly for חָסִיד, also for טָהוֹר, יָשָׁר, תָּמִים ;] 
religiously right, right­eous, pious, Holy: of men, Tite 1:8. Hébreux 7:26; by meton., ὁ. χεῖρας, 1 Timothée 2:8 (cf. Deutéronome 32:4); of God, Apocalypse 15:4 16:5; as subst., ὁ ὅ., of the Messiah, Actes 2:27 13:35" (LXX) ; τὰ ὅ. Δανεὶδ τ. πιστά (Field, Notes, 121), Actes 13:34 (LXX).†
SYN.: see: ἅγιος (cf. also DB, ii, 399.b; iv, 352.b, and ref. see word -ίως)

G3742.def:
ὁσιότης, -ητος, ἡ
(ὅσιος), [in LXX: Deutéronome 9:5 (יֹשֶׁר), 1 Rois 14:41, 3Ki.9:4 (תֹּם, תָּמִים), Proverbes 14:32, Wis.2:22 5:19 9:3 14:30 * ;] 
piety, holiness: assoc. with δικαιοσύνη, Luc 1:75, Éphésiens 4:24.†
SYN.: see: ἅγιος

G3743.def:
ὁσίως
(ὅσιος), 
adv., [in LXX: 3Ki.8:61, Wis.6:10 * ;] 
piously, holily: ὁ. καὶ δικαίως κ. ἀμέμπτως (on the distinction here between these synonyms, see M, Th., 24 f.), 1 Thessaloniciens 2:10.†

G3744.def:
ὀσμή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ὄζω), [in LXX chiefly for רֵיחַ ;] 
a smell, odour: Jean 12:3; metaphorically (EV, savour), 2 Corinthiens 2:14 2:16; of the effect of sacrifice (cf. נִיחוֹחַ רֵיחַ, Genèse 8:21, al., see: εὐωδία), ὀ. εὐωδίας, Éphésiens 5:2, Philippiens 4:18.†

G3747.def:
ὀστέον (Att.. contr. ὀστοῦν, -οῦ, and so Jo, l.with), -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for עֶצֶם ;] 
a bone: contr., ὀστοῦν (see supr.), Jean 19:36 (LXX); uncontr. (as in Hom., Hdt.), ὀστέα, Luc 24:39; ὀστέων, Matthieu 23:27, Hébreux 11:22.†

G3749.def:
ὀστράκινος -η, -ον
(ὄστρακον, an earthen vessel or potsherd), [in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶשׂ ;] 
made of clay, earthen: 2 Corinthiens 4:7, 2 Timothée 2:20.†

G3750.def:
ὄσφρησις, -εως, ἡ
(ὀσφραίνομαι, to smell), 
the sense of smell, smell­ing: 1 Corinthiens 12:17.†

G3751.def:
ὀσφύς, -ύος, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for מֹתֶן;, also for חָלַץ, etc. ;] 
the loin: Matthieu 3:4, Marc 1:6; metaphorically, περιζώννυσθαι (ἀναζ-) τ. ὀσφύας, Luc 12:35, Éphésiens 6:14, 1 Pierre 1:13; regarded, as by the Hebrews, as the seat of generative power, Hébreux 7:5, 10; metaphorically, καρπὸς τ. ὀσφύος, Actes 2:30

G3753.def:
ὅτε, temporal particle (correlat. of πότε, τότε), 
when; with indic., (so generally in cl., but also with optative, subjc.; LS, see word), most frequently with aor., Matthieu 9:25, Marc 1:32, Luc 4:25, Jean 1:19, Actes 1:13, Romains 13:11, Galates 1:15, Apocalypse 1:17, al.; with impf., Marc 14:12, Jean 21:18, Romains 6:20, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:4, al.; with pf., since, now that, 1 Corinthiens 13:11 (B, ἐγένομην); with praes., Marc 11:1, Jean 9:4, Hébreux 9:17, with fut. (Hom.; of a def. fut. as opposite to the indef. fut. of ὅταν with subjc.), Luc 17:22, Jean 4:21, 23 5:25 16:25, Romains 2:16 (T, txt., WH, mg.), 2 Timothée 4:3 (in all which instances, and with pres., Jo, l.with, ὅ. follows a subst. of time, and is equiv. to a rel. phrase, ἐν ᾧ or ᾗ).

G3754G.def:
ὅτι, 
conjc. (prop. neut. of ὅστις). 
__I. As conjc, introducing an objective clause, that; 
__1. after verbs of seeing, knowing, thinking, saying, feeling: Matthieu 3:9 6:32 11:25, Marc 3:28, Luc 2:49, Jean 2:22, Actes 4:13, Romains 1:13 8:38 10:9, Philippiens 4:15, Jacques 2:24, al.; elliptically, Jean 6:46, Philippiens 3:12, al. 
__2. After εἶναι (γίνεσθαι): defining a demonstr. or of person(s) pron., Jean 3:19 16:19, Romains 9:6, 1 Jean 3:16 al.; with pron. interrog., Matthieu 8:27, Marc 4:41, Luc 4:36, Jean 4:22 al.; id. elliptically, Luc 2:49, Actes 5:4, 9, al.; 
__3. Untranslatable, before direct discourse (ὅτι recitantis): Matthieu 7:23, Marc 2:16, Luc 1:61, Jean 1:20, Actes 15:1, Hébreux 11:18, al. (on the pleonastic ὡς ὅτι, see: ὡς).
__II. As causal particle, for that, because: Matthieu 5:4-12, Luc 6:20, 21, J0 1:30 5:27, Actes 1:5, 1 Jean 4:18, Apocalypse 3:10, al. mult.; διὰ τοῦτο ὅτι, Jean 8:47 10:17, al.; answering a question (διὰ τί), Romains 9:32, al.; οὐκ ὅτι . . . ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι, Jean 6:26 12:6.

G3754H.def:
ὅτι, 
conjc. (prop. neut. of ὅστις). 
__I. As conjc, introducing an objective clause, that; 
__1. after verbs of seeing, knowing, thinking, saying, feeling: Matthieu 3:9 6:32 11:25, Marc 3:28, Luc 2:49, Jean 2:22, Actes 4:13, Romains 1:13 8:38 10:9, Philippiens 4:15, Jacques 2:24, al.; elliptically, Jean 6:46, Philippiens 3:12, al. 
__2. After εἶναι (γίνεσθαι): defining a demonstr. or of person(s) pron., Jean 3:19 16:19, Romains 9:6, 1 Jean 3:16 al.; with pron. interrog., Matthieu 8:27, Marc 4:41, Luc 4:36, Jean 4:22 al.; id. elliptically, Luc 2:49, Actes 5:4, 9, al.; 
__3. Untranslatable, before direct discourse (ὅτι recitantis): Matthieu 7:23, Marc 2:16, Luc 1:61, Jean 1:20, Actes 15:1, Hébreux 11:18, al. (on the pleonastic ὡς ὅτι, see: ὡς).
__II. As causal particle, for that, because: Matthieu 5:4-12, Luc 6:20, 21, J0 1:30 5:27, Actes 1:5, 1 Jean 4:18, Apocalypse 3:10, al. mult.; διὰ τοῦτο ὅτι, Jean 8:47 10:17, al.; answering a question (διὰ τί), Romains 9:32, al.; οὐκ ὅτι . . . ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι, Jean 6:26 12:6.

G3756.def:
οὐ, before a vowel with smooth breathing οὐκ, before one with rough breathing οὐχ (but improperly οὐχ ἰδού, Actes 2:7, WH, mg.; cf. WH, Intr., §409; M, Pr., 44, 244), 
[in LXX for אֵין ,אַיִן ,לֹא ;] 
neg. particle, 
not, no, used generally with indic, and for a denial of fact (cf . μή); 
__1. absol. (accented), οὔ, no: Matthieu 13:29 Jean 1:21 21:5; οὒ οὕ, Matthieu 5:37 Jacques 5:12. 
__2. Most frequently negativing a verb or other word, Matthieu 1:25 10:26, 38, Marc 3:25 9:37, Jean 8:29, Actes 7:5, Romains 1:16, Philippiens 3:3, al.; in litotes, οὐκ ὀλίγοι (i.e. very many), Actes 17:4, al.; οὐκ ἄσημος, Actes 21:39; πᾶς . . . οὐ, with verb, (like Heb. כֹּל . . . לֹא), no, none, Matthieu 24:22, Marc 13:20, Luc 1:37, Éphésiens 5:5, al.; in disjunctive statements, οὐκ . . . ἀλλά, Luc 8:52 Jean 1:33 Romains 8:2o, al.; with 2 of person(s) fut. (like Heb. לֹא, with impf.), as emphatic prohibition, Matthieu 4:7, Luc 4:12, Romains 7:7, al. 
__3. With another negative, 
__(a) strengthening the negation: Marc 5:37, Jean 8:15 12:19, Actes 8:39, al.; 
__(b) making an affirmative: Actes 4:20, 1 Corinthiens 12:15. 
__4. With other particles: οὐ μή (see: μή); οὐ μηκέτι, Matthieu 21:19; with μή interrog., Romains 10:18, 1 Corinthiens 9:4, 5 11:22. 
__5. Interrogative, expecting an affirmative answer (Lat. nonne): Matthieu 6:26, Marc 4:21, Luc 11:40, Jean 4:35, Romains 9:21, al.

G3758.def:
οὐά, 
interj. 
of wonder or irony, ah! ha!: Marc 15:29.†

G3759.def:
οὐαί 
interj. of grief or denunciation, [in LXX for הוֹי, etc. ;] 
alas! woe! most frequently with dative of person(s) Matthieu 11:21 23:14, Marc 13:17 14:21, Luc 6:24-26 Ju 11, al.; with vocat. (nom.), Apocalypse 18:10, 16 18:19 (cf. Ésaïe 1:24, al.); with accusative, Apocalypse 12:12, before ἐκ, Apocalypse 8:13; with dative before ἀπό (see M, Pr., 246), Matthieu 18:7. As subst., 1 Corinthiens 9:16 (cf. Jérémie 6:4); ἡ οὐ., Apocalypse 9:12 11:14; pl., Apocalypse 9:12; οὐ., οὐ., οὐ., Apocalypse 8:13

G3760.def:
οὐδαμῶς
(οὐδαμός, not even one), 
adv., [in LXX: 2-4Mac.8* ;] 
in no wise, by no means: Matthieu 2:6 (OT).†

G3761.def:
οὐδέ, negative particle, related to μηδέ as οὐ to μή. 
__I. As conjc., and not, also not, neither, nor: Matthieu 6:15, Luc 16:31, Romains 4:15, al.; οὐ . . . οὐδέ, Matthieu 5:15 10:24, Marc 4:22, Luc 6:43, 44, Jean 6:24, Actes 2:27, Romains 2:28, al. (see Bl., §77, 10). 
__II. As adv., not even: Matthieu 6:29, Marc 6:31, Luc 7:9, 1 Corinthiens 5:1; οὐδὲ εἷς, Actes 4:32, Romains 3:10" (LXX) .

G3762.def:
οὐδείς, -δεμία, -δέν (also in WH, txt., the Hellenistic forms -θείς, -θέν, Luc 22:35 23:14, Actes 15:9 19:27 26:26, 1 Corinthiens 13:2, 2 Corinthiens 11:8; cf. BL, §6, 7; M, Pr., 56n, Thackeray, Gr., 58), related to μηδείς as οὐ to μή, 
no, no one, none: with nouns, Luc 4:24, Jean 10:41, Romains 8:1, al.; absol., Matthieu 6:24, Marc 3:27, Luc 1:61, Jean 1:18, Actes 18:10, Romains 14:7, al. mult.; with genitive partit., Luc 4:26, Jean 13:28, al.; neut., οὐδέν, Matthieu 10:26, al.; id. with genitive partit., Luc 9:36, Actes 18:17, al.; οὐδὲν εἰ μή, Matthieu 5:13, Marc 9:29, al.; with neg., strengthening the negation, Marc 15:4, 5 Luc 4:2, Jean 3:27, al.; adverbially, Actes 25:10, Galates 4:12, al.

G3763.def:
οὐδέ-ποτε, 
adv. [in LXX: Exode 10:6 (לֹא), etc. ;] 
never: Matthieu 7:23 9:33 26:33, Marc 2:12, Luc 15:29, Jean 7:46, Actes 10:14 11:8 14:8, 1 Corinthiens 13:8, Hébreux 10:1, 11. Interrog., Matthieu 21:16, 42, Marc 2:25 †

G3764.def:
οὐδέπω 
adv., [in LXX: Exode 9:30 (טֶרֶם)* ;] 
not yet: Luc 23:53, Jean 7:39 19:41 20:9, Actes 8:16.†

G3766.def:
οὐκοῦν 
adv. (οὔκουν, not therefore), 
with the negative element lost, therefore, so then: Jean 18:37.†

G3767.def:
οὖν, 
particle 
expressing consequence or simple sequence (never standing first in a sentence), wherefore, therefore, then: Matthieu 3:10, Luc 3:9, Jean 8:38, Actes 1:21, Romains 5:9, al.; in exhortations, Matthieu 3:8, Luc 11:35, Actes 3:19, Romains 6:12, al.; in questions, Matthieu 13:28, Marc 15:12, Jhn.8:[5], Romains 6:1, al.; continuing a narrative or resuming it after a digression, Matthieu 1:17, Luc 3:18, Jean 1:22 2:18 (and very frequently in this Gospel), Actes 26:22, al.; ἄρα οὖν (see: ἄρα); ἐπεὶ οὖν, Hébreux 2:14; οὖν with ptcp. (= ἐπεὶ οὖν), Actes 2:30, Romains 5:1, al.; ἐὰν οὖν (where οὖν rather in sense belongs to the apodosis), Matthieu 5:23, Luc 4:7, Jean 6:62, Romains 2:26, al.; ὡς οὖν, Jean 4:1, al.

G3768.def:
οὔπω 
neg. adv. of time, 
not yet: Matthieu 24:6, Marc 13:7, Jean 2:4 3:24 6:17, al.; with neg., Marc 11:2, Luc 23:53; interrog., Matthieu 16:9, Marc 4:40 8:17, 21

G3769.def:
οὐρά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
[in LXX for זָנָב ;] 
a tail: Apocalypse 9:10, 19 12:4.†

G3770.def:
οὐράνιος, -ον
(cl. usually -α, -ον), [in LXX: Deutéronome 28:12 A (שָׁמַיִם), etc. ;] 
of or in heaven, heavenly: Matthieu 5:48 6:14, 26 6:32 15:13 18:35 23:9, Luc 2:13, Actes 26:19.†

G3771.def:
οὐρανόθεν
(οὐρανός), 
adv., [in LXX: 4Ma.4:10 * ;] 
from heaven: Actes 14:17 26:13.†

G3772.def:
οὐρανός, -οῦ, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁמַיִם (hence, often pl., οἱ οὐ., see infr.) ;] 
heaven; 
__1. of the vault or firmament of heaven, the sky and the aerial regions above the earth: opposite to ἡ γῆ, Hébreux 1:10, 2 Pierre 3:5, 10; ὁ οὐ. καὶ ἡ γῆ, i.e. the world, the universe, Matthieu 5:18, Marc 13:31, Luc 10:21, Actes 4:24, Apocalypse 10:6, al.; ἀπ᾽ ἄκρων οὐ. ἕως ἄ. αὐτῶν (on the absence of art. aft. prep., see Bl, §46, 5), Matthieu 24:31; ὑπὸ τὸν οὐ., Actes 2:5, Colossiens 1:23; ὑψωθῆναι ἕως τοῦ οὐ., figuratively, Matthieu 11:23, Luc 10:15; σημεῖον ἐκ τοῦ οὐ., Matthieu 16:1, Marc 8:11, al.; αἱ νεφέλαι, Matthieu 24:30, al.; τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐ., Matthieu 6:26, Marc 4:32, al.; οἱ ἀστέρες τοῦ οὐ., Apocalypse 6:13, al.; pl. (οἱ) οὐ. (Bl., §32, 5), Matthieu 3:16, Marc 1:10, Jean 1:32, 2 Pierre 3:7, 13 al. 
__2. Of the abode of God and other blessed beings: of angels, Matthieu 24:36, Marc 12:25, Galates 1:8, Apocalypse 10:1, al.; of Christ glorified, Mrk.16:[19], Luc 24:51, Actes 3:21, Romains 10:6, al.; of God, Matthieu 5:34, Romains 1:18, al.; ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐ. (Dalman, Words, 184ff.), Matthieu 5:16 6:1, al.; θησαυρὸς ἐν οὐ., Matthieu 6:20, Marc 10:21, al. 
__3. By meton., 
__(a) of the inhabitants of heaven: Apocalypse 18:20 (cf. ib. 12:12, Job 15:15, Ésaïe 44:23); 
__(b) as an evasive reference to God, characteristic of later Judaism (Dalman, Words, 204ff.): Matthieu 21:25, Marc 11:30, Luc 15:18, Jean 3:27, al.; ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐ. (= τοῦ Θεοῦ); see: βασιλεία). 
βασιλεία, -ας, ἡ 
(βασιλεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מַמְלָכָה ,מַלְכוּת ;] 
__1. prop. abstract, sovereignty, royal power, dominion: Luc 1:33 22:29, Jean 18:36, Actes 1:6, Hébreux 1:8, 1 Corinthiens 15:24; λαβεῖν β., Luc 19:12, 15 Apocalypse 17:12; δοῦναι τὴν, ib. 17; ἔχειν β., ib. 18; ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τ. (εἰς τὴν) β., Matthieu 16:28, Luc 23:42; β. τ. θεοῦ, Apocalypse 12:10. 
__2. By meton., concrete (MM, Exp., x), 
__(a) a kingdom, the territory or people over whom the king rules (Esther 5:3, al.): Matthieu 4:8 12:25, 26 24:7, Marc 3:24 6:23, Luc 4:5, Hébreux 11:33, al.; 
__(b) the royal majesty (cf. our phrase His Majesty), the king himself (τ. σπέρμα τῆς β., 4Ki.11:1). 
__3. In LXX (Wis.6:5, Tob.13:1, al.), Targ. and NT, of the Messianic rule and kingdom, ἡ β. τ. θεοῦ, τ. οὐρανῶν (Heb. מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, Aram. מַלְכוּתָא דִשׁמַיָּא; see Dalman, Words, 91-147; Cremer, 132, 658), the kingdom of God (on the equivalence of the two phrases, see Dalman, op. cit., 93, 218f.); τ. θεοῦ, Matthieu 6:33 12:28, al.; τ. οὐρανῶν, Matthieu 3:2 4:17, al.; τ. Χριστοῦ (מַלִכוּת דִמְשִׁיחא, Targ. Jon. on Ésaïe 53:10), Éphésiens 5:5; τ. κυρίου, 2 Pierre 1:11, Apocalypse 11:15; τ. Δαυείδ, Marc 11:10; absol., ἡ β., Matthieu 4:23, Jacques 2:5, al. The kingdom is regarded as present: Matthieu 11:12, Luc 17:21, Romains 14:17, al.; as that which is to be consummated in the future, Matthieu 6:10, Marc 9:1, Jean 3:5, 2 Pierre 1:11, al. Noteworthy phrases are: ζητεῖν τὴν β., Matthieu 6:33; δέχεσθαι, Marc 10:15; κλρονομεῖν, Matthieu 25:34; διδόναι, Lk 12:32; παραλαμβάνειν, Hébreux 12:28; αὐτῶν (τοιούτων) εστὶν ἡ β., Matthieu 5:3, 10 19:14, Marc 10:14, Luc 18:16; διὰ τὴν β., Matthieu 19:12; ἕνεκεν τῆς β., Luc 18:29; εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, κηρύσσειν, διαγγέλλειν τὴν β., Luc 4:43 9:2, 60; ἤγγικεν ἡ β., Matthieu 3:2, Marc 1:15; κλεῖς τῆς β., Matthieu 16:10; κλείειν τὴν β., Matthieu 23:14; υἱοὶ τῆς β., Matthieu 8:12 13:38 (cf. Cremer, 132, 658).
\

G3775.def:
οὖς genitive, ὠτός, τό, 
[in LXX chiefly for אֹזֶן ;] 
the ear: Matthieu 13:16, Marc 7:33, Luc 22:50, 1 Corinthiens 2:9 12:16, 1 Pierre 3:12; ἐν τ. ὠσί, Luc 4:21; εἰς τ. ὦτα ἀκούεσθαι, Actes 7:57; γίνεσθαι, Luc 1:44; εἰσέρχεσθαι, Jacques 5:4; εἰς τ. οὖς ἀκούειν, Matthieu 10:27; πρὸς τ. οὖς λαλεῖν, Luc 12:3; τὰ ὦ. συνέχειν (MM, xviii), Actes 7:57. Metaphorical, of understanding, perceiving, knowing: Matthieu 13:16; ὁ ἔχων (εἴ τις ἔχει) οὖς ἀκουσάτω, Apocalypse 2:7, 11 2:17, 29 3:6, 13 13:9; ὁ ἔχων (ὃς ἔχει, εἴ τις ἔχει) ὦτα (ἀκούειν) ἀκουέτω, Matthieu 11:15 13:9, 43, Marc 4:9, 23 7:16 (R, mg.), Luc 8:8 14:35; τοῖς ὠ. βαρέως ἀκούειν, Matthieu 13:15 Actes 28:27" (LXX) ; ὦ. ἔχοντες οὐκ ἀκούειν, Marc 8:18; ὦ. τοῦ μὴ ἀκούειν, Romains 11:8; θέσθε εἰς τὰ ὦ., Luc 9:44; ἀπερίτμητος τοῖς ὠ., Actes 7:51.†

G3776.def:
οὐσία, -ας, ἡ
(οὖσα, fem. part. of εἰμί), [in LXX: Tob.14:13, 3Ma.3:28 * ;] 
substance, property: Luc 15:12-13.†

G3777.def:
οὔτε 
negative particle, related to μήτε as οὐ to μή, 
and not, neither, nor: οὐδεὶς . . . οὔτε, Apocalypse 5:4; οὐδὲ . . . οὔτε, Galates 1:12; οὔτε . . . καί, Jean 4:11; after a question with μή interrog., Jacques 3:12; οὔτε . . . οὔτε, neither . . . nor, Matthieu 6:20, Marc 12:25, Jean 4:21, Actes 15:10, Romains 8:38-39, Galates 5:6, al

G3779.def:
οὕτως, rarely (Bl., §5, 4; WH, App., 146f.) οὕτω, adv. 
(οὗτος), [in LXX chiefly for כֵּן ;] 
in this way, so, thus; 
__1. referring to what precedes: Matthieu 5:16 6:30, Marc 10:43 14:59, Luc 1:25 2:48 15:7, Jean 3:8, Romains 1:15, 1 Corinthiens 8:12, al.; οὕτως καί, Matthieu 17:12, Marc 13:29, al.; pleonastically, resuming a ptcp. (cl.; see Bl., §74, 6), Actes 20:11 27:17. 
__2. Referring to what follows: Matthieu 1:18 6:9, Luc 19:31, Jean 21:1, 1 Pierre 2:15; bef. quotations from OT, Matthieu 2:5, Actes 7:6, 1 Corinthiens 15:45, Hébreux 4:4. 
__3. C. adj. (marking intensity): Hébreux 12:21, Apocalypse 16:18; similarly with adv., Galates 1:6 (cl.). 
__4. As a predicate (Bl., §76, 1): Matthieu 1:18 9:33, Marc 2:1, 2 4:26, Romains 4:18 9:20, I Pe 2:15; οὕ ἔχειν (Lat. sic or ita se habere), Actes 7:1, al.; ἐκαθέζετο (as he was, without delay or preparation), Jean 4:6. 
__5. In comparison, with correlative adv.: καθάπερ . . . οὕ., Romains 12:4, 5 al.; καθὼς . . . οὕ., Luc 11:30, al.; οὕ. . . . καθώς, Luc 24:24, al.; ὡς . . . οὕ., Romains 5:15, al.; οὕ . . . ὡς, Marc 4:26, al; ὥσπερ . . . οὕ., Matthieu 12:40, al.; οὕ. . . . οὕ., 1 Corinthiens 7:7.

G3781.def:
ὀφειλέτης, -ου, ὁ
(ὀφείλω), 
a debtor: with genitive (of the amount), Matthieu 18:24. Metaphorical, of obligation or duty in general, with reference to favours received or injury done, etc.: Matthieu 6:12, Romains 1:14 8:12 15:27, Galates 5:3; of sinners, in relation to God (= Heb. חַיָּב; cf. Sir (Hébreux 8:5) (6)), Luc 13:4.†

G3782.def:
ὀφειλή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ὀφείλω), 
a debt: Matthieu 18:32; metaphorically, one's due: Romains 13:7, 1 Corinthiens 7:3 (found also in π.; see Deiss., BS, 221; MM, xviii).†

G3783.def:
ὀφείλημα, -τος, τό
(ὀφείλω), [in LXX: Deutéronome 24:10 (מַשָּׁאָה), I Esther 3:20, 1Ma.15:8 * ;] 
that which is owed, a debt: Romains 4:4; metaphorically (as Aram. חוֺבָא חוֺב), of sin as a debt, Matthieu 6:12.†

G3784.def:
ὀφείλω 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 15:2, Ésaïe 24:2 (נָשָׁה), Eze.18:7 (חוֹב), Wis.12:15, 20, al. ;] 
to owe, be a debtor: with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 18:28, Luc 7:41 16:7, Phm 18; id. with dative of person(s), Matthieu 18:28, Luc 16:5. Pass., to be owed, to be due: τ. ὀφειλόμενον, Matthieu 18:30, 34. Metaphorical: absol. (= Rabbinic חַיָּב; see McNeile, in l), Matthieu 23:16, 18; with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), Romains 13:8; with inf., to be bound or obliged to do (of. Westc., Epp. Jo., 50), Luc 17:10, Jean 13:14 19:7, Actes 17:29, Romains 15:1, 27, 1 Corinthiens 5:10 7:36 9:10 11:7 11:10, 2 Corinthiens 12:14, Éphésiens 5:28, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:3 2:13, Hébreux 2:17 5:3, 12, 1 Jean 2:6 Jn 3:16 Jn 4:11, 3Jn.8; ὤειλον συνίστασθαι, I ought to have been commended, 2 Corinthiens 12:11. In peculiar Aram. sense of having wronged one (see: όφείλημα; but of. also Inscr. ἁμαρτίαν ὀφείίλω, Deiss., BS, 225), with dative of person(s), Luc 11:4 (cf. προσ-οφίελω).†

G3785.def:
ὄφελον 2 aorist of ὀφείλω, without the augment (see M, Pr., 201n), used to express a fruitless wish; 
[in LXX (with aor. indic.): Exode 16:3 (נָתַן מִי), Nombres 14:2 Nombres 20:3 (לוּא), Psaumes 119:5 (אַחֲלַי), etc. ;] 
in cl. with an infin. (chiefly poët.), 
would that: with indic. aor., 1 Corinthiens 4:8; impf., 2 Corinthiens 11:1, Apocalypse 3:15; fut., Galates 5:12 (a practicable wish, see 131., 206 f., 220. The construction with indic. is only found in late writers.)†

G3786.def:
ὄφελος, -ονς, τό
(ὀφέλλω, to increase) [in LXX: Job 15:3 (יָעַל hi.)* ;] 
advantage, help: 1 Corinthiens 15:32, Jacques 2:14, 16.†

G3787.def:
ὀφθαλμο-δουλία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ 
(ὀφθαλμός, δοῦλος), 
eye-service: Éphésiens 6:6, Colossiens 3:22 (not found elsewhere).†

G3789.def:
ὄφις, -εως, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for נָחָשׁ ;] 
a serpent, snake: Matthieu 7:10 Marc 16:18, Luc 10:19 11:11, Jean 3:14, 1 Corinthiens 10:9, Apocalypse 9:19; as typical of wisdom and cunning, Matthieu 10:16 23:23, 2 Corinthiens 11:3 (cf. Genèse 31:1-55); of Satan (cf. Genèse 3:1, Wis.2:23-24, 4Ma.18:8), Apocalypse 12:9, 14 12:11 20:2.†

G3790.def:
ὀφρύς -ύος, ἡ
[in LXX: Lévitique 14:9 (עַיִן גַב) * ;] 
an eyebrow, the brow of a hill: Luc 4:29.†

G3791.def:
ὀχλέω, -ῶ
(ὄχλος), [in LXX: Tob.6:7, 3Ma.5:41 * ;] 
to move, disturb; hence, generally, to trouble, vex: pass., Actes 5:6 (act. absol., = pass., to be in a tumult, 3Mac, l.with; cf. ἐν-, παρ-εν-οχλέω, and see MM, xviii).†

G3792.def:
ὀχλο-ποιέω, -ῶ 
to gather a crowd, make a riot: Actes 17:5 (not elsewhere).†

G3793.def:
ὄχλος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX for הָמוֹן (chiefly in Da TH), קָהָל ,חַיִל, etc. ;] 
__1. a moving crowd or multitude of persons, a throng: Matthieu 9:23, Marc 2:4, Luc 5:1, Jean 5:13, al.; pl., Matthieu 5:1, Marc 10:1, Luc 3:7, and freq.; ὄ. ἱκανός, Marc 10:46, al.; τοσοῦτος, Matthieu 15:33; οὐ μετ᾽ ὄχλου, Actes 24:18; ἄτερ ὄχλου, Luc 22:6; πᾶς ὁ ὄ., Matthieu 13:2, Marc 2:13, al.; ὄ. πολύς, Matthieu 20:29, Marc 5:21, al.; ὁ πολὺς ὄ. (ὄ. π.), the populace, the common people, Marc 12:37 (Swete, in l.; Field, Notes, 37), Jean 12:9 (Westc, in l.). 
__2. (As also cl., opposite to δῆμος, which see, and cf. Tr., Syn., §xcviii), the populace, the common people (cf. ὁ πολὺς ὄ., supr.), Matthieu 14:5 21:26, Marc 12:12, Jean 7:12b; so with contempt (cl.), Jean 7:49. In a more general sense, a multitude: with genitive, ὀνομάτων (see: ὀ.), Actes 1:15; μαθητῶν, Luc 6:17, al.

G3794.def:
ὀχύρωμα, -τος, τό
(ὀχυρόω, to fortify, make firm), [in LXX for מִבְצָר, etc. ;] 
a stronghold, fortress (Psaumes 89:40, Nahum 3:12, 14 al.); in LXX and NT, also metaphorically of that in which confidence is placed (Proverbes 10:29 21:22, al.): 2 Corinthiens 10:4.†

G3795.def:
ὀψάριον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of ὄψον, (1) cooked meat; (2) a relish or dainty, esp. fish, cf. MGr. τὸ ψάρι, fish; in comic poets and late prose writers only) [in LXX: Tob.2:2 א (Β, ὄψον)* ;] 
fish: Jean 6:9, 11 21:9-10, 13 †

G3796.def:
ὀψέ, adv. of time 
[in LXX: Genèse 24:11, Exode 30:8 (עֶרֶב, עֶרֶב בֵּין), Jérémie 2:23; τὸ ὀ., Ésaïe 5:11 (נֶשֶׁף)* ;] 
__1. long after, late. 
__2. late in the day, at evening (opposite to πρωί); in late writers used almost as an indecl. noun (see MM, xviii): Marc 11:11, 19 13:35. 
__3. C. genitive, late in or on; and, in late writers also after (M, Pr., 72 f.), a sense which seems to be required in Matthieu 28:1.†

G3797.def:
ὄψιμος, -ον
(ὀψέ), [in LXX: Deutéronome 11:14, Proverbes 16:15, Osée 6:4 (3), Joël 2:23, Zacharie 10:1, Jérémie 5:24 (מַלְקוֹשׁ), Exode 9:32 (אָפִיל)* ;] 
poët. and late for ὄψιος, late: ὑετὸς ὄ., 
the latter rain (see DB, see word "rain"), with ellipsis of ὑετός (see WM, 740), Ja 57.†

G3798.def:
ὄψιος, -α, -ον
(ὀψέ), 
late: ἡ ὥρα, Marc 11:11 (Rec., WH, mg.). In late writers, ἡ ὀψία (sc. ὥρα), as subst., evening 
[in LXX: Jdth.13:1*]: 
Matthieu 8:16 14:15, 23 16:2 20:8 26:20 27:57, Marc 1:32 4:35 6:47 14:17 15:42, Jean 6:16 20:10.†

G3799.def:
ὄψις, -εως, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for מַרְאֶה ;] 
__1. the act of seeing, the sense of sight. 
__2. face, countenance: Jean 11:44, Apocalypse 1:16. 
__3. appear­ance: κατ᾽ ὄ. κρίνειν (see MM, xviii), Jean 7:24.†
